newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NINE ARRESTED AFTER CROWD TROUBLE AT QPR MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NINE ARRESTED AFTER CROWD TROUBLE AT QPR MATCH.

text.p: Play was suspended for almost 20 minutes after fighting broke out among rival Queens Park Rangers and Portsmouth fans at an English first division match at Loftus Road on Saturday.
A spokesman for Scotland Yard said nine fans had been arrested for public order offences. Four people were injured in the disturbances at the stadium in west London, but none were seriously hurt.
"Our understanding is that three fights broke out and quickly escalated with people getting onto the pitch to escape from the fighting," he said.
"The referee had to suspend play, but it was resumed when police officers were confident order had been restored. Three men and one woman were hurt, but none had serious injuries."

Referee Kevin Lynch was forced to order players off after 53 minutes when fans, some protecting young children, spilled on to the pitch to escape from the fighting that initially broke out in a family section of the Ellerslie Road stand.
Eye-witnesses said the trouble broke out when a group of around 20 Portsmouuth fans, who were in a section of the crowd reserved for QPR fans, began scuffling with the home supporters.
Stewards and police were quickly on the scene, but fights then broke out in two other stands and it took the authorities almost 20 minutes to bring the situation under control. QPR won the game 2-1.
Portsmouth manager Terry Fenwick, who used to play for QPR, told reporters afterwards the fans who caused the problem were pathetic individuals.

"I don't know whether it was our fans or theirs who were responsible. I hope it wasn't our fans. Our players need their support not the sort of thing that went on out there today. It's pathetic really, I thought we had got away from all this aggravation."
QPR boss Stewart Houston said he felt it was important to get his players back in the dressing room.
"I said to the players that there was a lot of tension in the crowd but that we must not show it when we went back out there. It certainly affected Portsmouth a lot more than us."
Under current legislation any fan convicted of public order offences at a football ground can be banned from matches for life.
The trouble at QPR continues a recent worrying trend and follows recent outbreaks of violence at Birmingham, Leicester and Chesterfield.
It also comes just days after Manchester United fans were left injured, battered and bruised in clashes with Portuguese police when their side played Porto in the European Cup on Wednesday.
